subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <cstdlib> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 40-odd symbols across 8 family headers plus the umbrella. THE WHOLE MODULE IS RE-EXPORTS, and that is the correct design rather than a shortfall: every function is a contract with the C runtime, not library logic. malloc's blocks must return to the runtime's free, atexit's handlers must land on the runtime's list, getenv reads the process environment, the multibyte functions read the active locale. Same reasoning as <new> and <typeinfo>; the opposite of <bitset>, which re_std owns outright. Two symbols are conditional and are OMITTED where unavailable rather than redirected to a near-equivalent with different semantics: aligned_alloc (MSVC, older Apple) and the quick_exit pair (Apple). Granularity is by family rather than by symbol -- a documented exception, since every symbol shares the single dependency <cstdlib> and per-symbol headers would narrow nothing.
legend_blurb: <cstdlib> provides C runtime services: allocation, process termination, string-to-number conversion, search and sort, integer arithmetic, pseudo-random numbers and multibyte conversion.

symbols.name: atof / atoi / atol / atoll
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. NO ERROR REPORTING: atoi("hello") is 0, indistinguishable from atoi("0"), and out-of-range input is undefined behaviour rather than a diagnosable error. Surfaced for completeness and for porting, not as a recommendation -- prefer the strto* family, or from_chars from C++17. atoll is a C++11 addition. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. The C++11 library additions in the same file (atoll, strtof, strtold, strtoll, strtoull, _Exit, llabs, lldiv, lldiv_t) are now gated individually, so the C++98 names stay reachable at C++98.

symbols.name: strtod / strtof / strtold
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. The result depends on the C locale's decimal point and on the platform's floating-point parsing; a reimplementation would be a second parser with different last-digit rounding. Sets errno to ERANGE and reports an end pointer. strtof and strtold are C++11. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. symbols.name: rand / srand (+ RAND_MAX)
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. Specifically: the sequence is the runtime's, so code that seeds with srand and reads with a re_std::rand must be drawing from the same generator. KNOWN LIMITATIONS, none fixable from here -- hidden global state so not thread-safe; quality unspecified and poor on several runtimes; `rand() % n` biased unless n divides RAND_MAX+1; RAND_MAX only guaranteed to reach 32767. A better generator would be a DIFFERENT generator and would break the interoperation that is the reason for re-exporting. <random> (priority 40) is the right answer. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. The C++11 library additions in the same file (atoll, strtof, strtold, strtoll, strtoull, _Exit, llabs, lldiv, lldiv_t) are now gated individually, so the C++98 names stay reachable at C++98.

symbols.name: malloc / calloc / realloc / free
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. A block from one malloc must return to the matching free, so substituting an implementation would corrupt every allocation crossing a library boundary. NOT the C++ allocation path: no constructors or destructors run, and mixing with new/delete on the same pointer is undefined. realloc returns null on failure WITHOUT freeing the original, so assigning the result over the only surviving pointer leaks the block. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. The C++11 library additions in the same file (atoll, strtof, strtold, strtoll, strtoull, _Exit, llabs, lldiv, lldiv_t) are now gated individually, so the C++98 names stay reachable at C++98.

symbols.name: aligned_alloc
symbols.notes: GATED. C++17 adopted it from C11, but MSVC's runtime has never provided it and Apple's libc gained it only in macOS 10.15. Where absent the name is simply NOT DECLARED rather than aliased to _aligned_malloc -- that function must be released with _aligned_free rather than free, so it is not a drop-in, and a redirect would turn a compile error into a heap corruption. D_RE_STD_HAS_ALIGNED_ALLOC reports availability and is user-overridable.
symbols.failure_reason: Requires C++17 and a runtime that declares it; absent on MSVC and on Apple before macOS 10.15. Omitted rather than approximated -- see notes.

symbols.name: abort / exit / _Exit / atexit (+ EXIT_SUCCESS / EXIT_FAILURE)
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. The registered-handler lists live in the runtime. THE PATHS DIFFER IN WHAT THEY RUN: exit runs static destructors, then atexit handlers, then flushes and closes streams; _Exit runs nothing; abort runs nothing and terminates abnormally (SIGABRT). Buffered output is LOST on the last two -- intended, but it surprises people. _Exit is a C++11 addition. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. The C++11 library additions in the same file (atoll, strtof, strtold, strtoll, strtoull, _Exit, llabs, lldiv, lldiv_t) are now gated individually, so the C++98 names stay reachable at C++98.

symbols.name: quick_exit / at_quick_exit
symbols.notes: GATED. Both are C++11 and both are absent from Apple's libc to this day. Where missing the names are not declared rather than redirected to _Exit: silently substituting a function that skips the at_quick_exit handlers would turn a compile error into a shutdown that quietly does less than the author asked for. Runs the at_quick_exit list only -- no static destructors, no stream flushing -- which is the point when destructor order is unsafe.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor, and additionally absent on Apple platforms, where the pair is omitted rather than approximated.

symbols.name: getenv / system
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. Both reach outside the process. getenv returns a BORROWED pointer into the environment block -- must not be freed or written through, may be invalidated by a later setenv, and is not thread-safe against concurrent modification. system IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY: any part of the argument built from untrusted input is a shell injection, and there is no portable escaping routine, which is why re_std offers none -- a helper that looked like it made the call safe would be worse than the raw function. setenv and putenv are deliberately ABSENT: not in the standard's <cstdlib>, and the POSIX and Windows forms differ in signature and ownership. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. The C++11 library additions in the same file (atoll, strtof, strtold, strtoll, strtoull, _Exit, llabs, lldiv, lldiv_t) are now gated individually, so the C++98 names stay reachable at C++98.

symbols.name: qsort / bsearch
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. Prefer re_std::sort and re_std::lower_bound on every axis: type-safe, comparison inlined rather than called through a pointer, any random-access range rather than a contiguous array, and O(n log n) worst case where qsort's complexity is unspecified. Surfaced for C interoperation. THE CLASSIC TRAP: a comparator returning `*a - *b` is correct for small values and overflows into a wrong SIGN for large ones, so the sort silently produces a wrong order rather than failing. qsort is also not stable. symbols.name: abs / labs / llabs
symbols.notes: Re-exported despite being four characters of arithmetic, for one reason: OVERLOAD IDENTITY. The set of std::abs overloads visible at a call site decides which wins, and a separate re_std::abs would create a second, differently populated set -- reintroducing the classic abs(-3.5) yielding 3 bug in the library meant to prevent it. WHICH OVERLOADS YOU GET DEPENDS ON WHAT ELSE IS INCLUDED: the floating-point ones live in <cmath> (priority 118, not implemented), and a using-declaration captures whatever is visible when this header is parsed. abs on a double is therefore not portable until <cmath> lands. abs(INT_MIN) is undefined -- the magnitude is not representable; re_std::ratio rejects INTMAX_MIN for the same reason. llabs is C++11. symbols.name: div / ldiv / lldiv (+ div_t / ldiv_t / lldiv_t)
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. Quotient and remainder in one call, truncating toward zero. Since C++11 that is also what / and % do, so the family's original reason for existing has largely lapsed. lldiv and lldiv_t are C++11. symbols.name: mblen / mbtowc / wctomb / mbstowcs / wcstombs (+ MB_CUR_MAX)
symbols.notes: Re-exported, not reimplemented: this is a contract with the C runtime rather than library logic, and a second implementation would be a disconnected copy of state the process already has one of. Every one reads the current C locale, which is process-global state no library-side reimplementation could consult. THREE OF THEM CARRY HIDDEN SHIFT STATE (mblen, mbtowc, wctomb), making them non-reentrant and unsafe to call from two threads even on different strings -- the <cwchar> restartable forms take an explicit mbstate_t and should be preferred (priority 129, not implemented). 'Multibyte' here is NOT UTF-8 unless the active locale says so; in the default C locale a UTF-8 string is mangled rather than converted, and setlocale lives in <clocale> (priority 117). MB_CUR_MAX is the CURRENT locale's maximum and on most runtimes is not even a constant; buffers want <climits>'s MB_LEN_MAX. UNGATED 2026-08-25: this family was behind a whole-file C++11 gate for no reason -- the functions are C++98. The C++11 library additions in the same file (atoll, strtof, strtold, strtoll, strtoull, _Exit, llabs, lldiv, lldiv_t) are now gated individually, so the C++98 names stay reachable at C++98.
